titre: The Eiffel Tower very nearly got dismantled in 1909
accroche: Built to last only twenty years, the Eiffel Tower escaped dismantling only by becoming, almost in spite of itself, a giant radio antenna.
contenu_vulgarise:
The contract signed on January 8, 1887, between Gustave Eiffel and the French state grants the engineer commercial rights to his tower during the 1889 Exposition Universelle (World's Fair), and then for twenty more years. After that, on January 1, 1910, the structure is to revert in full ownership to the City of Paris, with no clause guaranteeing that it stay standing. There is a precedent: in 1906, the City has the Galerie des Machines torn down, even though it was the largest building in the world at the time, for lack of any use to find for it.

## A tower in search of a purpose

Aware from the outset that the symbol alone would not be enough to save his tower, Eiffel sets about finding a scientific justification for it. Wireless telegraphy, a nascent technology of the 1890s, offers him one. On November 5, 1898, Eugène Ducretet establishes the first radio link in Morse code from the tower, to the Panthéon, four kilometers away. The army takes an interest in the technology in turn: Captain Gustave Ferrié of the engineering corps sets up his team at the foot of the south pillar and pushes back the range of transmissions year after year, up to six thousand kilometers in 1908. In 1909, a permanent station is set up beneath the Champ-de-Mars.

The tower's strategic value is now proven, and not only for the army: starting in 1910, the Paris Observatory uses the same transmitter to broadcast the exact time every day to ships at sea, within a radius of five thousand kilometers, helping to unify the world's clocks around a common time. On January 1, 1910, the very date on which his original concession was due to expire, Gustave Eiffel obtains an extension of seventy years. This is no mere formality: during the First World War, the radio station installed at its summit intercepts German communications. In March 1918, a coded radiogram is picked up there and then deciphered in three days by Georges Painvin, a graduate of the École Polytechnique, making it possible to thwart a decisive German offensive.

## What this changes

The Eiffel Tower that is presented today as an eternal monument of Paris was therefore never designed to be one: it escaped dismantling, unlike the Galerie des Machines, which nonetheless surpassed it in size, only by becoming a scientific and military instrument at the precise moment its lease was expiring. What the world's most photographed silhouette owes to its looks, it owes just as much to a radio transmitter installed at its summit a year before a contract expired.

repere.texte: In 1909, a permanent wireless telegraphy station is installed beneath the Champ-de-Mars. The tower's strategic value is confirmed, which earns Gustave Eiffel an extension of his concession for seventy years from January 1, 1910, the very date on which it was originally due to revert to the City of Paris.

carte.punch: With no clause guaranteeing its survival in 1910, the Eiffel Tower owed its extension to radio.
carte.idee: The 1887 contract gave Gustave Eiffel twenty years of operation after the 1889 Exposition: on January 1, 1910, the tower was due to revert to the City of Paris, with no clause guaranteeing its survival. Equipped with a radio station of strategic value, it obtains a seventy-year extension that very day.

quiz.question: Why was Gustave Eiffel's concession on his tower extended by seventy years, starting January 1, 1910?
choix: A petition signed by several thousand Parisians had persuaded the City to give up on demolition
The cost of dismantling had turned out to be higher than the cost of maintaining the existing structure
The tower had become a wireless telegraphy station whose strategic value the army had demonstrated
Gustave Eiffel had bought the Champ-de-Mars land from the City of Paris a few years earlier
quiz.explication: It was the demonstration, carried out notably by Captain Gustave Ferrié, of the tower's strategic value as a very-long-range wireless telegraphy antenna that convinced the state to extend the concession by seventy years, on precisely the day it was originally due to expire. Neither a petition, nor a cost calculation, nor a land purchase played any part.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the Eiffel Tower risk if it found no use before its concession expired, as the 1906 precedent shows?
choix: It risked being sold to a foreign power
It risked being destroyed, as the Galerie des Machines was in 1906 for lack of any use
It risked being turned into a museum unrelated to its original use
It risked being repainted a different color by the City of Paris
quiz_supplementaire.explication: There is a precedent: in 1906, the City has the Galerie des Machines torn down, even though it was the largest building in the world at the time, for lack of any use to find for it.
